intended_object: The intersection ⋂ᵢ 𝒪_{vᵢ} of the valuation rings of an arbitrary family of valuations (vᵢ) on a field K, i.e. the subring {x ∈ K | vᵢ(x) ≤ 1 for all i}. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the membership lemma that follows the definition.
explanation:
The body is the infimum in the lattice of subrings of the subrings `(val i).valuationSubring.toSubring`. That is exactly the intersection of the valuation rings. The lemma right after it, `mem_intersectionSubring_iff`, confirms that x belongs to it iff `val i x ≤ 1` for every i.

Degenerate case: for an empty family the result is all of K (`⊤`), which is the standard convention for an empty intersection.

The setting is the natural one. Valuation rings of valuations on a field are the classical objects here, and the module's later results (weak approximation, residue fields, localizations) are about fields.

Two possible generalizations, neither a real narrowing:
- **Common value group Γ₀.** All valuations in the family take values in the same Γ₀. This is the usual Mathlib style, and the subring depends only on the valuations up to equivalence, so it loses no real generality.
- **Rings instead of fields.** Mathlib's `Valuation.integer` would make the same intersection meaningful over any ring, but the topic of this file is valuation rings in a field.

Mathlib has no dedicated definition for the intersection of the valuation rings of a family. It only offers the generic `iInf` on subrings, which this definition uses directly.
